extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism adjudication from local XML/PDF/database packet only

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Pap12-6 has direct source-supported bacterial membrane permeabilization evidence from dye leakage, membrane depolarization, ONPG permeability, and SEM morphology assays.
supported_values: 100% leakage from bacterial-mimicking LUVs at 16 μM Pap12-6
22% leakage from mammalian-mimicking LUVs at 16 μM Pap12-6
44% E. coli membrane depolarization at 16 μM Pap12-6
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct membrane mechanism is strongest for Pap12-6; mechanism for other analogues is not promoted beyond comparative activity/structure context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectroscopy supports membrane-associated alpha-helical structure for Pap12 peptides, with Pap12-5 and Pap12-6 showing high helicity in membrane-mimetic environments.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper also references supplementary Fig. S3 for predicted structure; the local packet does not contain the external DOCX supplement, so no Fig. S3 details were extracted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Pap12-6 has source-supported anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-stimulated macrophage and TLR4 reporter systems.
supported_values: TNF-alpha inhibition of 74.3% and 83.9% at 10 and 20 μM
IL-6 inhibition of 39.7% and 59.6% at 10 and 20 μM
SEAP inhibition of 31% at 25 μM and 95% at 100 μM
mechanism_claims.limitations: Classified as immunomodulatory signaling evidence; not converted into a direct antimicrobial membrane claim.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Pap12-6 has in vivo efficacy support in an E. coli K1 sepsis model, including survival, tissue bacterial growth, endotoxin, cytokine, and organ-damage marker outcomes.
supported_values: 100% survival at 24 h after 10 mg/kg pretreatment
organ bacterial-growth reductions reported up to 67.4%
mechanism_claims.limitations: In vivo efficacy is supporting biological context, not a direct molecular antimicrobial mechanism by itself.
